newsitem.title: THAILAND: Hollywood appeals for release of Burma comedian.
newsitem.headline: Hollywood appeals for release of Burma comedian.

text.p: A group of prominent U.S. entertainers appealed for the release of a popular Burmese comedian who was imprisoned after a political performance last year, a human rights organisation said on Wednesday.

Human Rights Watch Asia said in a statement received in Bangkok that a group of top American comedians had signed letters sent to top Burmese military government officials urging the release of Par Par Lay.

The letters, signed by actors including Carl Reiner, Ted Danson, Paul Reiser, Mike Farrell and Mary Steenburgen, argued Par Par Lay had been jailed for exercising his internationally guaranteed rights to freedom of expression.

The comedian was part of a well-known Burmese musical troupe which performed at an independence day celebration at the Rangoon home of Nobel Peace laureate and opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi on January 4, 1996.

After returning home to Burma's second city Mandalay, Par Par Lay and 11 others in the group were detained. His performance satirised the ruling military junta and its record of corruption, Human Rights Watch Asia said.
The comedian and other actors in the troupe were sentenced to seven years' hard labour under the Emergency Provisions Act for "spreading false news".
In letters sent to Burmese prime minister General Than Shwe and top junta official Lieutenant-General Khin Nyunt, the Hollywood comedians urged Par Par Lay's immediate release.

"We are deeply troubled about reports that Par Par Lay's health has seriously deteriorated since his arrest," the letters said. "We want to personally express our concern and urge you to take immediate action to unconditionally release from detention one of our colleagues."
Human Rights Watch Asia said it had received information that Par Par Lay had been singled out for particularly brutal treatment at the labour camp, and he was weak and seriously ill.
The rights group said Par Par Lay and another comedian were constantly shackled to an iron bar that makes it difficult to sleep or do work.

Suu Kyi said in January she had a hard time finding actors to participate in her annual independence day celebration at her home because she and the actors feared possible reprisals from the government.
